name: Zung.AI core banking platform
demand: Kenya alone had 357 regulated SACCOs, 7,806,340 members and 669 branches in 2025, according to KNBS data sourced from SASRA: https://www.knbs.or.ke/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026-Economic-Survey.pdf. A broader, non-equivalent ceiling is the global credit-union and financial-cooperative movement: about 61,838 organisations in 93 countries serving nearly 420 million members at year-end 2025: https://www.woccu.org/newsroom/releases/WOCCU_Releases_Latest_Statistical_Report_on_the_Global_Credit_Union_Movement. These populations are not software-buyer counts. Public search-volume and app-install figures are unverified. Flippa displays 40,536 monthly page views for the listing, but those are not product demand or unique visitors: https://flippa.com/13438355-profitable-ai-powered-core-banking-saas-faas-for-saccos-mfis-banks-40k-monthly-visitors-1-churn-includes-10-revenue-fintech-ecosystem-sub-brands-bundled
prices: Zung.AI's own site quotes Growth at $349/month for 5,000 members and separately shows $6,588/year for 10,000 members; confirm the applicable plan and terms: https://zung.ai/. Competitor list prices include Kwara Premium from KSh 30,000/month excluding VAT, with Enterprise pricing custom: https://kwara.com/pricing/; and Peshap NODi at KES 25,000/month for up to 2,000 members or KES 55,000/month for up to 15,000, with Enterprise custom-priced: https://peshapcloud.com/pricing.

revenue_proof.claim: The live Flippa page displays $5,685 monthly profit, 82% margin, 18 active subscribers and 1% overall churn; its description separately says about $25,000 ARR and 15 paying institutions. Flippa says its team reviewed revenue, primary expenses and traffic, and that Xero is connected. The underlying statements, invoices, customer roster and churn calculation are not publicly shown, so this is listing-level evidence, not independently reproducible proof: https://flippa.com/13438355-profitable-ai-powered-core-banking-saas-faas-for-saccos-mfis-banks-40k-monthly-visitors-1-churn-includes-10-revenue-fintech-ecosystem-sub-brands-bundled
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: Unverified: the listing does not disclose the dates of the revenue transactions, churn period or Flippa review.

revenue_proof.claim: The seller's stated $25,000 ARR does not reconcile publicly with the displayed $5,685 monthly profit: if that profit were sustained for 12 months, it would annualize to $68,220, greater than the stated ARR. The listing's revenue verification badge does not expose the dated records needed to resolve this.
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: Unverified: no underlying transaction period is stated.

copy_speed: Evidence of recent competition: Mambu announced Intelligent Core, combining core banking, payments and agentic AI, on 2 September 2026: https://mambu.com/en/insights/press/mambu-launches-intelligent-core. Tiwala's site says its microfinance core-banking pilot launches September 2026; whether that pilot went live is unverified: https://tiwa.la/. A press report says Pitron FinOS launched for Ethiopian SACCOs and MFIs on 23 July 2026: https://www.fsxbusiness.com/pitron-brings-core-banking-technology. These launches show adjacent products can appear quickly; their adoption and direct overlap with Zung's customers are unverified.
platform_risk: Zung's site claims AWS Nairobi hosting is available now, alongside SOC 2 Type II and PCI DSS Level 1 claims; certification evidence and partner agreements need inspection: https://zung.ai/legal-center/. AWS currently lists Nairobi as an announced Local Zone with a request-interest step, not as an available location on its Local Zones page, so the in-country hosting claim needs documentary confirmation: https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/localzones/locations/. The site also claims M-Pesa, WhatsApp and many other integrations; contracts, API access, account ownership and transfer consent are unverified: https://zung.ai/. Kenya's ODPC describes service providers processing data for an institution as data processors, making data-processing contracts and compliance evidence material to diligence: https://www.odpc.go.ke/faqs/.
defensible_asset: The plausible moat is switching cost if customers really run member records, ledgers, loan workflows and integrations on the platform; the listing claims 15 institutional customers and six-week migrations, but provides no customer references or migration evidence publicly: https://flippa.com/13438355-profitable-ai-powered-core-banking-saas-faas-for-saccos-mfis-banks-40k-monthly-visitors-1-churn-includes-10-revenue-fintech-ecosystem-sub-brands-bundled. A proprietary compiled-data asset, maintained jurisdictional rules engine and network effect are unverified. Customer financial data is sensitive and cannot be treated as a transferable moat without customer rights, contracts and applicable privacy permissions.
build_effort: Buying may avoid a greenfield build, but operating the acquired platform still appears technically and operationally demanding: ledger correctness, migrations, integrations, security, regulatory changes, customer support and incident response. Zung's site claims 50+ integrations and 90-day hypercare, but these claims and actual support burden are unverified: https://zung.ai/. No code review, deployment records, ticket history or staffing evidence is publicly available.
channel: Use inbound SEO and region-specific compliance content, paid search/display configured for local rules, software directories and marketplaces, integration listings, and opt-in partner referrals or co-marketing with sector and implementation partners. Keep all referrals solicited and avoid unsolicited email, SMS, DMs and calls. UK ICO guidance distinguishes subscriber types and requires consent for marketing email or text to individuals; check each recipient country's rules and each ad platform's policies: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/how-do-we-comply-with-the-pecr-electronic-mail-marketing-rules/.
automation_reason: Rough estimate of the share of all company work, not measured: 35%. Zung's marketing describes AI for scoring, compliance and collections, but that automates customer workflows, not necessarily the seller's own sales, bespoke migrations, support, security reviews or regulatory assurance; the site also claims 90-day hypercare: https://zung.ai/. No owner time logs, staff roster, support-ticket volumes or internal automation evidence are disclosed in the listing: https://flippa.com/13438355-profitable-ai-powered-core-banking-saas-faas-for-saccos-mfis-banks-40k-monthly-visitors-1-churn-includes-10-revenue-fintech-ecosystem-sub-brands-bundled.
listing_check: Reopened 23 Oct 2026: the live page displays asking price $101,600, monthly profit $5,685, 82% margin, 1.5x profit multiple, 18 active subscribers and 1% overall churn; the description says about $25,000 ARR and 15 paying institutions. At the displayed ask and profit, annualizing the monthly profit gives $68,220 and a calculated 1.49x price/profit multiple. Flippa says it reviewed revenue, primary expenses and traffic and that Xero is connected. Churn period and dated financial source records are unverified. Owner hours are unverified. Transferability of source code, customer contracts, data-processing agreements, domains, cloud accounts, integrations and payment/communications accounts is unverified. Seller dependence is unverified; the seller says they plan to move to new ventures. Flippa says buyers and sellers must establish transferability and obtain any needed third-party consents: https://support.flippa.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000976136-Does-Flippa-help-with-asset-business-transfer. The live page also says site age is six years while the description says established June 2025.
moat_assessment: Potentially meaningful switching costs if the claimed live ledgers, customer workflows, integrations and migration history are real. Not yet evidenced enough to count as a proven moat: public customer references, cohort retention, contracts and transfer rights are missing. No compiled proprietary dataset, maintained regulatory rules engine or functioning network effect is demonstrated by the listing. Zung's current website makes much larger customer-scale claims than the listing, which need independent verification: https://zung.ai/; https://flippa.com/13438355-profitable-ai-powered-core-banking-saas-faas-for-saccos-mfis-banks-40k-monthly-visitors-1-churn-includes-10-revenue-fintech-ecosystem-sub-brands-bundled.
desk_test: No-cost, one-day seller-mediated diligence gate before any offer: request NDA/read-only Xero access plus dated bank statements and invoice exports for the latest 12 complete months; rebuild revenue, profit, refunds, churn and customer concentration, reconciling the 15 institutional customers against 18 subscribers and the $25,000 ARR against monthly profit. Ask the seller to arrange warm reference calls with paying institutions to confirm actual usage, renewal, support and migration effort. In the same session inspect source-code/IP ownership, customer and data-processing contract assignment clauses, cloud-region evidence and certification reports. If access or reconciliation is refused, stop. Flippa itself advises buyers to review financials and request dashboard access, and assigns transfer checks to buyer and seller: https://flippa.com/13438355-profitable-ai-powered-core-banking-saas-faas-for-saccos-mfis-banks-40k-monthly-visitors-1-churn-includes-10-revenue-fintech-ecosystem-sub-brands-bundled; https://support.flippa.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000976136-Does-Flippa-help-with-asset-business-transfer.
red_flags: The live figures do not establish either hard operating constraint: owner time is unknown and my rough 35% automation estimate is below the required 50%. The $25,000 ARR statement conflicts with the displayed monthly profit if that profit is representative; churn's period is missing. The listing's six-year site age conflicts with its June 2025 establishment date, and its 15 institutions/18 subscribers differ sharply from Zung's website claims of 340+ or 500+ institutions and 12M+ members; these are unverified marketing claims, not corroborated customer evidence: https://flippa.com/13438355-profitable-ai-powered-core-banking-saas-faas-for-saccos-mfis-banks-40k-monthly-visitors-1-churn-includes-10-revenue-fintech-ecosystem-sub-brands-bundled; https://zung.ai/. Seller dependence, actual customer retention, transfer consents and the AWS Nairobi hosting claim remain unresolved. Do not treat the cheap listed multiple as validated until the desk test passes.
